sentences.text: Kourisodon is an extinct genus of mosasaur named for its Greek meaning of 'razor tooth'. The type species, K. puntledgensis, was a small mosasaur reaching an estimated length of about 3.75 meters. It belongs to the subfamily Mosasaurinae within the family Mosasauridae.
A complete 12-foot-3-inch replica of the type specimen is displayed at the Canadian Fossil Discovery Centre in Manitoba.

Kourisodon was first classified in the tribe Leiodontini but is now classified as a clidastine. Fossils have been found on Vancouver Island in Canada and in the Izumi Group of Japan. A fragmentary skeleton from Shikoku Island, Japan, found in 2005 was assigned to an unnamed species of Kourisodon.
K. puntledgensis lived in a Pacific environment alongside elasmosaurids, turtles, and other mosasaurs, but no polycotylids were present.
Researchers suggest that a Japanese specimen with longer maxillary teeth might represent a second, unnamed species of Kourisodon.

Kourisodon fossils date from the Late Santonian stage to the Late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous. Kourisodon lived between 85.7 and 66 million years ago, spanning the Santonian to Maastrichtian periods.
